Render an env to YAML files under outDir.manifests, with an input-hash cache, atomic writes, and a timing report.

import { Aside } from "@/components/docs"

`konfig build <env>` loads the env entry, runs the `AppOfApps` (or `Bundle`) program, renders every manifest through the `RenderContext`, and writes one YAML file per resource plus one Argo CD `Application` per app. A build whose inputs have not changed since the last run writes nothing.

## Usage

```bash
konfig build <env> [--log text|json] [--verbose] [--no-cache]
                   [--cluster <name>] [--k8s-version <ver>] [--flag k=v ...]
```

## Arguments

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | required | Env name to build (for example `prod`). Resolved via `envs.<env>.entry` or `<root>/env/<env>.ts`. |

## Flags

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--log` | `text` | Output format for the report line: `text` or `json`. |
| `--verbose` | `false` | Wrap the render in an Effect span named `konfig.render.<env>` so tracing output shows per-render timing. |
| `--no-cache` | `false` | Skip the input-hash check and force a fresh render (debugging, first build). |
| `--cluster` | unset | Shared render flag, see [CLI overview](/konfig.ts/docs/cli/overview/). Adds a `<cluster>` directory level to the output path. |
| `--k8s-version` | unset | Shared render flag. |
| `--flag k=v` | unset | Shared render flag, repeatable. |

## Output layout

The output root is `<configDir>/<root>/<outDir.manifests>/<env>` (plus `/<cluster>` when `--cluster` is set). Inside it:

- One directory per app named after the app (`Application.name`), containing `<Kind>-<name>.yaml` for every rendered resource. `.` and `/` in names are replaced with `-` in filenames. `RawYaml` output (Helm releases, sops passthrough) is split on real YAML document boundaries into the same per-resource files.
- One directory named after the app-of-apps program (`"apps"` unless you set `name`), containing `Application-<app>.yaml` for every child app.

```text
.generated/manifests/prod/
├── apps/
│   ├── Application-api.yaml
│   └── Application-postgres.yaml
├── api/
│   ├── Deployment-api.yaml
│   └── Service-api.yaml
└── postgres/
    └── ...
```

Writes are atomic: everything is staged under `<outDir>.tmp`, then the live directory is removed and the staging directory renamed into place. Files are written with mode `0600`. Apps render with a concurrency of 4 to keep the number of `helm` and `sops` subprocesses bounded.

## Cache

Before rendering, `build` computes a SHA-256 over the decoded `konfig.json`, the render context (`cluster`, `k8sVersion`, sorted `flags`), the env entry file, every file under `root` (skipping `node_modules`, `dist`, `.konfig`), and every path matched by `cacheInclude`. The hash and an output hash are stored in `<configDir>/.konfig/cache/<env>-<ctxKey>.json`, where `ctxKey` is a digest of the render context, so different `--cluster`/`--flag` combinations do not share a slot.

A cache hit requires all of: the input hash matches, the recorded output directory is the one this invocation would write, the directory exists, and its on-disk contents still hash to the recorded output hash. Editing or deleting a generated file by hand is therefore a miss, and the next build rewrites the tree. The hash is conservative: touching any file under `root` invalidates it.

<Aside type="tip">
Add `.konfig/` to `.gitignore`. It holds only the build cache and the Helm tarball cache.
</Aside>

## Report

Text mode prints `Rendering env 'prod'...` followed by one report line: `Wrote 42 file(s) to /abs/out/prod` with the render and write times in milliseconds, or on a hit `Cached`, with a note that the env's inputs are unchanged and the file count at the output directory.

`--log json` prints a single JSON object per run:

```json
{"env":"prod","files":42,"outDir":"/abs/out/prod","renderMs":812,"writeMs":9,"totalMs":821,"cached":false}
```

## Exit codes and errors

The process exits non-zero when the program fails. Common tagged errors: `ConfigNotFound`, `ConfigParseError`, `EnvEntryNotFound`, `EnvLoadError` (missing or non-Effect default export), any render error from your modules (for example `HelmVersionTooLow`, `HelmDigestMismatch`, unbound secrets), `WriteEnvError`, `BuildCacheError`.

## Example

```bash
konfig build prod                        # first run renders and writes
konfig build prod                        # second run: Cached, inputs unchanged
konfig build prod --cluster eu-west-1    # separate output dir and cache slot
konfig build prod --no-cache --log json  # force render, machine-readable report
```
Every field of konfig.json and images.json, with types, defaults, and which commands read them.

import { Aside, Snippet } from "@/components/docs"

`konfig.json` is the project file the CLI discovers by walking up from the current directory. It is decoded with the strict `KonfigConfig` schema from `@konfig.ts/core` (`decodeKonfigConfigEffect`): unknown keys are an error, so a typo in a field name fails the command instead of being ignored. All relative paths resolve against the directory that contains the file (`configDir`).

## Fields

| Field | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | `string` | required | Directory (relative to `konfig.json`) that holds your env entries, modules, and charts. `build` hashes everything under it for the cache. |
| `envs` | `Record<string, { entry: string }>` | required (may be `{}`) | Env name to entry file, relative to `root`. Envs not listed fall back to `<root>/env/<name>.ts`. |
| `outDir.manifests` | `string` | required | Where `build` writes, relative to `root`. Files land in `<root>/<outDir.manifests>/<env>[/<cluster>]/`. |
| `diff.baseline` | `string` | unset | Baseline manifest tree for `konfig diff`, relative to `root`; the env name is appended. `diff` fails with `DiffBaselineMissing` when absent. |
| `cacheInclude` | `string[]` | `[]` | Extra files, directories, or glob patterns (relative to `konfig.json`) hashed into the build cache on top of `root`, for inputs that live outside the konfig root. |
| `cluster` | `string` | `"cluster.ts"` | Path of the cluster module, relative to `root`. |
| `modules` | `string` | `"modules"` | Path of the modules directory, relative to `root`. |
| `charts` | `string` | `"charts"` | Path of the chart definitions directory, relative to `root`. |
| `crd.outDir` | `string` | `".generated/crd"` | Destination for generated CRD types (declarative; the CLI reads `KONFIG_CRD_OUT_DIR`, see below). |
| `helm.cacheDir` | `string` | `".konfig/helm-cache"` | Helm tarball cache directory (declarative; the CLI reads `KONFIG_HELM_CACHE`). |
| `helm.minVersion` | `string` | `"3.16.0"` | Minimum `helm` version (declarative; the CLI reads `KONFIG_HELM_MIN_VERSION`, and `Helm.release` takes its own `minVersion` option). |
| `services.outFile` | `string` | unset | Reserved for the services layer; validated only. |
| `services.globalPaths` | `string[]` | `[]` | Reserved for the services layer; validated only. |
| `clusters.<name>` | `{ registry?, ingressClass?, storageClass?, repositoryUrl? }` | unset | Per-cluster values, all optional strings. |

The CLI commands read `root`, `envs`, `outDir.manifests`, `diff.baseline`, and `cacheInclude`. The remaining fields are validated so a project can declare them in one place, but no `konfig` command reads them today. In particular `crd extract`, `crd verify`, and `helm fetch` take their paths from environment variables, not from `konfig.json`:

| Variable | Default | Used by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KONFIG_CHARTS_DIR` | `infra/k8s-konfig/charts` (resolved from cwd) | `crd`, `helm fetch`: directory of chart registry modules |
| `KONFIG_HELM_CACHE` | `.konfig/helm-cache` (resolved from cwd) | `crd`, `helm fetch`, and `Helm.release` at render time |
| `KONFIG_CRD_OUT_DIR` | `.generated/crd` (resolved from cwd) | `crd`: output directory for generated `.ts` files |
| `KONFIG_HELM_MIN_VERSION` | `3.16.0` | `crd`, `helm fetch`: preflight `helm version` check |

<Aside type="caution">
`clusters.<name>` in `konfig.json` is not what `--cluster` reads. `--cluster` only sets `ctx.cluster` on the `RenderContext` and changes the output directory; your env entry decides what to do with it (the full-stack example keeps its per-cluster overlays in `infra/cluster.ts`).
</Aside>

Generate TypeScript types from the CustomResourceDefinitions shipped in your Helm charts, and verify the committed output has not drifted.

import { Aside } from "@/components/docs"

`konfig crd` turns the CRDs bundled with your Helm charts into TypeScript types so custom resources can be authored with editor support. `extract` writes the files; `verify` regenerates them into a temp directory and fails when the committed copies differ.

## Usage

```bash
konfig crd extract --release <id> | --all
konfig crd verify
```

## Flags (`extract`)

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--release <id>` | unset | Chart release id to extract. |
| `--all` | `false` | Extract for every chart in the registry. |

Exactly one of `--release` or `--all` is required; passing neither prints `Specify --release <id> or --all` and fails with `MissingCrdFlags`. `verify` has no flags or arguments.

## What it reads

Both subcommands read their locations from environment variables, not from `konfig.json` (see [konfig.json](/konfig.ts/docs/cli/configuration/) for the table): the chart registry from `KONFIG_CHARTS_DIR` (default `infra/k8s-konfig/charts`), the tarball cache from `KONFIG_HELM_CACHE` (default `.konfig/helm-cache`), the output directory from `KONFIG_CRD_OUT_DIR` (default `.generated/crd`), and the minimum Helm version from `KONFIG_HELM_MIN_VERSION` (default `3.16.0`).

The registry is every `.ts` file in the charts directory whose name does not start with `_`. Each file is imported and scanned for an export carrying the `_konfigHelmRelease: true` marker; that object's `repo`, `chart`, `version`, optional `id` (defaults to the file name without `.ts`), and optional `digest` form one registry entry, decoded against strict patterns for chart names, versions, and `http(s)`/`oci` repo URLs so shell metacharacters never reach `helm`.

```ts title="infra/k8s-konfig/charts/postgres.ts"
export const chart = {
  _konfigHelmRelease: true,
  id: "postgres",
  repo: "https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami",
  chart: "postgresql",
  version: "16.0.0",
  digest: "sha256:..."
}
```

## Behaviour

- Runs `helm version --short` first and fails with `HelmVersionTooLow` when `helm` is missing or older than the minimum.
- For each release: `helm pull --repo <repo> <chart> --version <v> --untar` into a scoped temp directory and read `crds/*.yaml`; then pull the tarball into the cache (skipped when `<cache>/<chart>-<version>.tgz` exists) and run `helm template <chart> <tgz> --include-crds --no-hooks`. Both sources are parsed and de-duplicated by CRD name.
- For every `CustomResourceDefinition` the first version's `openAPIV3Schema` is compiled with `json-schema-to-typescript` into an exported `<Resource>Input` type (the resource part of the CRD name, PascalCased), followed by a comment naming the CRD, group, and versions. A schema that fails to compile falls back to `Record<string, unknown>`.
- Output is `<outDir>/<id>.ts`, starting with a `// Generated by @konfig.ts/cli` header line marking it as generated. A chart without CRDs gets a stub file with the header and `export {}`.
- `verify` regenerates every registry entry into a temp directory and compares byte-for-byte with `<outDir>/<id>.ts`. A committed file that lacks the generated header is reported as `<id>.ts (missing generated header)`.

<Aside type="note">
The generated types are inputs for `Manifest.make` from `@konfig.ts/core`, which produces a `RawYaml` resource at render time. There is no runtime schema validation attached to them.
</Aside>

## Exit codes and errors

- `ReleaseNotFound { releaseId }` for an unknown `--release`; the message lists available ids.
- `MissingCrdFlags` when neither flag is given.
- `CrdDrift { drifted }` from `verify`, after printing `CRD drift detected in: ...` and `Run konfig crd extract --all to regenerate`.
- `HelmVersionTooLow`, `ChartRegistryError`, `ChartRegistryEntryDecodeError`, `CrdInputDecodeError`, `CrdExtractError { chart, cause }`.

## Example

```bash
KONFIG_CHARTS_DIR=infra/charts konfig crd extract --all
konfig crd verify      # in CI: non-zero exit when .generated/crd is stale
```
Structural diff of a rendered env against the baseline tree configured in diff.baseline, with Secret data redacted and Helm noise stripped.

import { Aside } from "@/components/docs"

`konfig diff <env>` renders the env in memory and compares it, file by file and document by document, against the YAML tree at `<root>/<diff.baseline>/<env>`. Comparison is structural: it parses YAML on both sides and compares values, so key order, quoting style, and whitespace never show up as changes.

## Usage

```bash
konfig diff <env> [--format summary|detail|json]
                  [--cluster <name>] [--k8s-version <ver>] [--flag k=v ...]
```

## Arguments

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | required | Env to diff. |

## Flags

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--format` | `summary` | `summary` prints one line per changed file; `detail` adds per-document `left:`/`right:` YAML; `json` prints the full `DiffResult`. |
| `--cluster`, `--k8s-version`, `--flag` | unset | Shared render flags, see [CLI overview](/konfig.ts/docs/cli/overview/). |

## Behaviour

- Requires `diff.baseline` in `konfig.json`; otherwise the command fails with `DiffBaselineMissing` before rendering.
- The left side is every `.yaml` file under the baseline directory (recursively, keyed by relative path). The right side is the in-memory render keyed by its path relative to the output directory. Files present on only one side are reported as `+ <file>` (new in render) or `- <file>` (only in baseline).
- Multi-document files are matched by identity, `kind|namespace|name`, not by position, so reordering documents is not a change. Single-document files are compared as one value.
- Both sides are normalised before comparison: `null` and `undefined` object values are dropped, the `helm.sh/chart` label and `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: Helm` label are removed, and the `meta.helm.sh/release-name` / `meta.helm.sh/release-namespace` annotations are removed. This keeps a Helm-managed baseline comparable to a konfig render.
- For `kind: Secret`, every value under `data` and `stringData` is replaced with `<redacted>` on both sides before comparing and printing. Changed keys are still detected (a key added or removed changes the map); changed values are not, and secret material never reaches the terminal.

## Exit codes and errors

- Exit `0` and an `OK` line (`env '<env>' matches baseline`) when nothing differs.
- Non-zero with `DiffNonEmpty` after printing the diff when anything differs, so the command works as a CI gate.
- `DiffBaselineMissing` when `diff` is not configured; config and render errors as in [konfig build](/konfig.ts/docs/cli/build/).

<Aside type="note">
`konfig diff` compares against a committed baseline tree, not against a live cluster. To compare against what `build` last wrote, point `diff.baseline` at your `outDir.manifests` directory.
</Aside>

## Example

```bash
konfig diff prod
# ~ api/Deployment-api.yaml
# + api/ConfigMap-feature-flags.yaml

konfig diff prod --format detail
konfig diff prod --format json > diff.json
```
Preview, write, and drift-check the Dockerfile and Dockerfile.dev generated from a workspace's docker.ts spec.

import { Aside, Snippet } from "@/components/docs"

`konfig docker` is the CLI surface of `@konfig.ts/docker`. Each app in the monorepo declares one `docker.ts` spec; the command resolves the app's transitive workspace closure from the root `package.json` workspaces and emits a production multi-stage `Dockerfile` plus a single-stage `Dockerfile.dev`, with no hand-maintained `COPY` lists.

## Usage

```bash
konfig docker preview <target> [--prod-only] [--dev-only]
konfig docker write   <target> [--out-dir <dir>] [--prod-only] [--dev-only] [--force]
konfig docker diff    <target> [--format summary|detail|json]
```

## Arguments

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | required | Workspace directory relative to the cwd (for example `apps/api`). `<target>/docker.ts` is imported and its default export must be a `Docker.app(...)` value. |

## Flags

| Command | Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `preview`, `write` | `--prod-only` | `false` | Only emit the production `Dockerfile`. |
| `preview`, `write` | `--dev-only` | `false` | Only emit `Dockerfile.dev`. |
| `write` | `--out-dir <dir>` | `<target>` | Destination directory, relative to the cwd. |
| `write` | `--force` | `false` | Overwrite a destination file even if it is not konfig-managed. |
| `diff` | `--format` | `summary` | `summary`, `detail`, or `json`, same formatter as `konfig diff`. |

## The spec

<Snippet file="apps/api/docker.ts" lang="ts" title="apps/api/docker.ts" />

`Docker.app({ target, runner, dev? })` is the entrypoint. `runner.copy` takes atoms from `Docker.copy`: `builderArtifact(src, dst)`, `workspaceSource(name)`, `workspaceSourceAll()`, `path(src, dst, opts?)`. `Docker.runtime.bun({ alpine? })` and `Docker.runtime.node({ alpine? })` pick the runtime image family (defaulting from the detected package manager, `alpine` defaults to `true`); `Docker.pm`, `Docker.build`, `Docker.healthcheck`, `Docker.user`, and `Docker.platform` cover the remaining knobs. See the [package README](https://github.com/DwieDave/konfig.ts/tree/main/packages/docker) for the full atom table.

The target's `package.json` must set `engines.<runtime>` (for example `"engines": { "bun": "1.3.5" }`); that version becomes the runner image tag. Missing it fails with `EngineVersionMissing`.

## Behaviour

- The monorepo root is found by walking up from the target until a `package.json` with `workspaces` (or a `pnpm-workspace.yaml`) is found; otherwise `MonorepoRootNotFound`. All `COPY` paths are relative to that root, so **the Docker build context must be the monorepo root**: `docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile .` from the root.
- Production is a four-stage build, `base` (runtime image pinned to `engines.<runtime>`), `deps` (installs from the full workspace set), `builder` (copies only the target's closure and runs the build), `runner` (non-root, copies only what the spec declares; `runner.production: true` re-installs prod-only deps). Dev is `base` then `dev`.
- Every emitted file starts with a header: `# konfig-managed: @konfig.ts/docker`, `# spec: <path>`, `# hash: sha256:...`. `write` refuses to overwrite a file that lacks the marker unless `--force` is given (`DockerWriteRefused`), skips the write when the managed content is identical (`unchanged <path>`), and writes atomically via a `.tmp.<pid>` rename.
- `preview` prints the production Dockerfile, then `# ---- Dockerfile.dev ----` and the dev one, to stdout.
- `diff` compares on-disk files with what would be emitted. Matching header hashes short-circuit; otherwise a structural diff is printed and the command fails with `DiffDrift { target, kind }`. Success prints an `OK` line: `<target> matches`.

<Aside type="note">
`docker` does not read `konfig.json`. It needs a TypeScript-capable runtime to import `docker.ts`, and it never builds, pushes, or tags images.
</Aside>

## Exit codes and errors

`SpecImportError`, `SpecNotADockerApp` (default export is not a `Docker.app` value), `DockerWriteRefused`, `DockerWriteError`, `DiffDrift`, and the `AnyDockerError` union from `@konfig.ts/docker` (`MonorepoRootNotFound`, `EngineVersionMissing`, `CircularWorkspaceDep`, `WorkspaceNotFound`, `UnsupportedPm`, ...).

## Example

```bash
konfig docker preview apps/api --prod-only
konfig docker write apps/api            # apps/api/Dockerfile + Dockerfile.dev
konfig docker diff apps/api             # CI gate
docker build -f apps/api/Dockerfile .   # context = monorepo root
```
Print an ASCII graph of the workspace dependency closure for one package, or the whole monorepo.

`konfig graph [target]` renders the workspace dependency graph that `@konfig.ts/docker` uses to compute build closures. Without a target it draws the whole monorepo; with one it draws that package's closure. It reads only `package.json` files, so it runs under plain Node.

## Usage

```bash
konfig graph [target] [--with-dev] [--full] [--width <n>]
```

## Arguments

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `target` | unset | Workspace directory (relative path such as `apps/api`) or package name (`@example/api`). Omit to render the whole monorepo. |

## Flags

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--with-dev` | `false` | Also draw `devDependencies` edges, annotated with `▽`. |
| `--full` | `false` | Show every direct edge. By default transitively implied edges are hidden (A→C is dropped when A→B→C exists). |
| `--width <n>` | `stdout.columns` or `100` | Override the detected terminal width. |

## Behaviour

- Finds the monorepo root by walking up from the cwd to a `package.json` with `workspaces` (or `pnpm-workspace.yaml`), then loads every workspace and its `package.json`.
- Nodes are workspaces; edges are `dependencies` and `peerDependencies` (runtime) and `devDependencies` (dev) whose spec uses the `workspace:` or `link:` protocol and points at another workspace. Non-workspace packages never appear.
- Runs a cycle check first. A cycle fails the command with `CircularWorkspaceDep` and prints `error: workspace cycle detected: a → b → a`.
- Dev edges are only drawn and only considered for the cycle check with `--with-dev`.
- Nodes that define a `build` script are marked so you can see which packages the `builder` stage will compile.

## Exit codes and errors

- `GraphTargetNotFound` when `target` matches neither a workspace name nor a relative directory; stderr lists the available workspace names.
- `CircularWorkspaceDep { cycle }` on a dependency cycle.
- `MonorepoRootNotFound` when no workspace root is found above the cwd.

## Example

```bash
konfig graph                          # whole monorepo
konfig graph apps/api --with-dev      # api's closure, including dev edges
konfig graph @example/api --full --width 140
```
Pre-fetch every registered Helm chart tarball into the local cache so renders and CRD extraction run offline.

import { Aside } from "@/components/docs"

`konfig helm` groups Helm chart management. It currently has one subcommand, `fetch`, which downloads every chart in the registry into the tarball cache ahead of time. Use it to warm CI caches or to make later `konfig build` and `konfig crd` runs independent of chart repositories.

## Usage

```bash
konfig helm fetch --all
```

## Flags (`fetch`)

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--all` | `false` | Fetch all charts into the local cache. Required; without it the command prints `Specify --all to fetch all charts` and fails with `MissingAllFlag`. |

## Behaviour

- Reads the same environment-variable configuration as `konfig crd`: registry directory `KONFIG_CHARTS_DIR` (default `infra/k8s-konfig/charts`), cache `KONFIG_HELM_CACHE` (default `.konfig/helm-cache`), minimum version `KONFIG_HELM_MIN_VERSION` (default `3.16.0`). See [konfig crd](/konfig.ts/docs/cli/crd/) for the registry file format.
- Runs `helm version --short` and fails with `HelmVersionTooLow` when `helm` is absent or too old.
- For every registry entry prints `Fetching <chart>@<version>...` and runs `helm pull --repo <repo> <chart> --version <version> --destination <cache>`, unless `<cache>/<chart>-<version>.tgz` already exists.
- Ends with `Done. Cache at <cache>`.

<Aside type="caution">
`helm fetch` does not verify digests. Digest verification happens at render time: `Helm.release({ digest })` in `@konfig.ts/core` hashes the cached tarball on every pull and every cache hit and fails with `HelmDigestMismatch` when the bytes changed. Render-time cache entries are keyed as `<chart>-<version>-<digest12>.tgz` inside the same `KONFIG_HELM_CACHE` directory.
</Aside>

## Exit codes and errors

`MissingAllFlag`, `HelmVersionTooLow { required, found }`, `ChartRegistryError`, `ChartRegistryEntryDecodeError`, and process failures from `helm pull`.

## Example

```bash
KONFIG_HELM_CACHE=~/.cache/konfig-helm konfig helm fetch --all
```

`konfig --help` lists the subcommands, `konfig <command> --help` lists arguments and flags, and `konfig --version` prints the package version. The CLI depends on Effect 4 (release candidate) and `@effect/platform-node`; the package pins the exact build it was compiled against, see the [README requirements](https://github.com/DwieDave/konfig.ts/tree/main/packages/cli#requirements).

## Runtime requirement

Most commands `import()` your `.ts` sources at runtime: `konfig build prod` loads the env entry, which pulls in your modules, `docker.ts` specs, and chart files. `konfig` therefore needs a TypeScript-capable runtime:

- Bun (recommended): runs `.ts` with no flags.
- Node >= 23.6: native type stripping.
- Node 22.6 to 23.5: pass `--experimental-strip-types`.
- `tsx`: `tsx node_modules/.bin/konfig ...`.

Commands that load sources: `build`, `validate`, `diff`, `crd extract`, `crd verify`, `helm fetch` (chart registry files), and `docker` (the `docker.ts` spec). Commands that only touch JSON or `package.json` files and run under plain Node: `set` and `graph`.

## Configuration discovery

`build`, `validate`, `diff`, and `set` walk up from the current working directory until they find a `konfig.json`. The directory containing that file becomes `configDir`; every relative path in the config (`root`, `outDir.manifests`, `diff.baseline`, env entries) resolves against it. When no file is found the command fails with `ConfigNotFound`; a file that does not decode against the schema fails with `ConfigParseError`. See [konfig.json](/konfig.ts/docs/cli/configuration/) for every field.

## Env entry resolution

An env is a named render target (`prod`, `staging`). Its entry module is:

1. `envs.<NAME>.entry` from `konfig.json`, joined onto `<configDir>/<root>`, when the env is declared.
2. Otherwise `<configDir>/<root>/env/<NAME>.ts`.

The entry's default export must be an Effect program, normally `AppOfApps.entrypoint(AppOfApps.fromModules({ ... }))` from `@konfig.ts/argocd`. A `Bundle` set program is also accepted. A missing file fails with `EnvEntryNotFound`; a module without a default export, or whose default export is not an Effect, fails with `EnvLoadError`.

## Shared render flags

`build`, `validate`, and `diff` accept the same three flags. They are folded into the `RenderContext` your modules receive.

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--cluster <name>` | unset | Target cluster name when one env spans several clusters. Surfaces as `ctx.cluster`; `build` writes into `<outDir>/<env>/<cluster>/`. |
| `--k8s-version <ver>` | unset | Target Kubernetes version (for example `1.31`). Surfaces as `ctx.k8sVersion` and shapes `apiVersion` picks. |
| `--flag k=v` | unset | Free-form key/value pairs. Repeatable; merged into one map read via `ctx.flags.get(k)`. |

```bash
konfig build prod --cluster eu --k8s-version 1.31 --flag canary=true --flag region=eu-central-1
```

<Aside type="note">
The cluster, version, and flags are part of the build cache key, so `konfig build prod` and `konfig build prod --cluster eu` keep separate cache slots.
</Aside>

Update one image reference in images.json with a schema-validated read and write, the CI-side half of image promotion.

`konfig set <env> <app> <image>` rewrites a single entry in `<root>/images.json`. It exists so a CI pipeline can promote a freshly built image with one command and a follow-up `konfig build` picks it up.

## Usage

```bash
konfig set <env> <app> <image>
```

## Arguments

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | required | Env key in `images.json` (for example `prod`, `staging`). |
| `app` | required | App key under `envs.<env>`. |
| `image` | required | Full image reference (for example `ghcr.io/<org>/<app>:<sha>`). |

There are no flags.

## Behaviour

- Locates `konfig.json` by walking up from the cwd, then reads `<configDir>/<root>/images.json`.
- Parses the file as JSON and decodes it with the strict `ImagesConfig` schema (`{ envs: Record<env, Record<app, string>> }`); unknown top-level keys are rejected.
- Fails when `env` is not present in `envs`; the error lists the known env names. Adding a new env is a deliberate edit, not something `set` does implicitly.
- `app` does not have to exist yet: an unknown app key is added under the env. There is no separate error for unknown apps.
- Builds the new config, decodes it again against the schema, and writes it back with tab indentation and a trailing newline (`JSON.stringify(cfg, null, "\t")`), matching the repo's `images.json` formatting so the diff is one line.
- Logs `set <env>.<app> = <image>` on success. Nothing is rendered; run `konfig build <env>` afterwards.

## Exit codes and errors

- `SetUnknownEnv { env, known }` when the env key is missing (also printed as `unknown env '<env>'. Known: a, b`).
- `ImagesFileError { path, cause }` for a missing or unreadable file, invalid JSON, or a schema failure on read or write.
- `ConfigNotFound` / `ConfigParseError` when `konfig.json` cannot be resolved.

## Example

A typical CI step after pushing an image:

```bash
konfig set prod api ghcr.io/example/api:sha-${GITHUB_SHA::7}
konfig build prod
git add infra/images.json .generated/manifests/prod
git commit -m "promote api to ${GITHUB_SHA::7}"
```

See [konfig.json](/konfig.ts/docs/cli/configuration/) for the `images.json` shape and the `imagesFor` / `requireImage` helpers that read it inside modules.
Render an env in memory, check every document's Kubernetes envelope, and optionally run kubeconform in strict mode.

`konfig validate <env>` renders the env exactly like `build` but keeps the result in memory. It then checks every YAML document structurally and, with `--strict`, hands the rendered tree to `kubeconform` for schema validation.

## Usage

```bash
konfig validate <env> [--strict] [--ignore-missing-schemas]
                      [--cluster <name>] [--k8s-version <ver>] [--flag k=v ...]
```

## Arguments

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `env` | required | Env name to validate. |

## Flags

| Name | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--strict` | `false` | Additionally run `kubeconform -summary -strict <dir>` over the rendered manifests. Requires `kubeconform` on `PATH`. |
| `--ignore-missing-schemas` | `false` | Append `-ignore-missing-schemas` to the kubeconform invocation, for CRDs the bundled schema set does not know. |
| `--cluster`, `--k8s-version`, `--flag` | unset | Shared render flags, see [CLI overview](/konfig.ts/docs/cli/overview/). |

## Behaviour

- Structural validation parses each rendered file with the YAML parser and decodes every non-null document against a Kubernetes envelope schema: `apiVersion: string`, `kind: string`, `metadata.name` matching the RFC 1123 label pattern, optional `metadata.namespace` with the same pattern, optional string maps for `labels` and `annotations`. Deeper fields are left to kubeconform.
- Every issue is printed to stderr as `<file> (doc <n>) <path>: <message>`; a YAML parse failure is reported as one issue for `doc 0`.
- On success it prints an `OK` line: `env '<env>': <n> file(s) pass structural validation`.
- `--strict` runs kubeconform against the directory `build` would write to. Pass/fail is decided by the exit code, not by scraping stdout. `--k8s-version` only affects your render (`ctx.k8sVersion`); it is not forwarded to kubeconform.
- Nothing is written to disk and the build cache is not consulted or updated.

## Exit codes and errors

- `StructuralValidationFailed { env, issueCount }` after any envelope issue; the issues are already on stderr.
- `KubeconformNotFound` when the binary cannot be spawned. The message reads `kubeconform binary not found`, asks you to install it for `--strict` validation, and includes the attempted command line (`kubeconform -summary -strict <dir> ...`).
- `KubeconformReportError { stdout, stderr }` when kubeconform exits non-zero; its output is included in the message.
- The same config, entry, and render errors as [konfig build](/konfig.ts/docs/cli/build/).

## Example

```bash
konfig validate prod
konfig validate prod --strict --ignore-missing-schemas
```
SecretRef, ConfigMapRef, PvcRef, ServiceAccountRef, BuiltImageRef and PortName; where @konfig.ts/k8s demands them and what that catches.

import { Aside, Snippet } from "@/components/docs"

Kubernetes links resources by plain strings: an env var names a Secret, a volume names a ConfigMap, a Service names a container port. `@konfig.ts/k8s` replaces those strings with branded types at every link, so a reference to something nobody created, or created in the wrong namespace, fails to type-check.

## The ref types

All refs are `string & { [Brand]: ... }`; the runtime value is the plain name and serializes to YAML unchanged.

| Ref | Type parameters | Produced by |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `SecretRef<N, K, Ns>` | name, key union, namespace | `Secret.make(...).ref`, `Secret.bind(...).ref`, `Environment.bind(...).members.X.ref`, `yield* Dep.Secret(name)` |
| `ConfigMapRef<N, K>` | name, key union | `ConfigMap.make(...).ref`, `yield* Dep.ConfigMap(name)` |
| `ServiceAccountRef<N>` | name | `ServiceAccount.make(...).ref`, `yield* Dep.ServiceAccount(name)` |
| `PvcRef<N>` | name | `yield* Dep.Pvc(name)`, `PvcRef.of(name)` |
| `BuiltImageRef<App>` | app name | `yield* Dep.Image(app)`, `BuiltImageRef.of({ app, registry, tag })` |
| `PortName<N>` | port name | `Port.make({ name, ... })`, `Port.ref(name)` |

`Secret.make` and `ConfigMap.make` infer `K` from the keys of `data` / `stringData`, so `EnvVar.fromConfigMap({ ref: featureFlags.ref, key: "NEW_UI" })` only accepts keys that exist. Renaming a key in the ConfigMap breaks every consumer at compile time.

Escape hatches exist for genuinely external resources: `SecretRef.of(name)`, `ConfigMapRef.of(name)`, `ServiceAccountRef.of(name)`, `PvcRef.of(name)`. They mint a ref without any provider, so use them only for objects managed outside konfig.ts.

## Enforcement points

The following inputs take a branded ref and reject a raw string:

- `EnvVar.fromSecret` / `EnvVar.fromSecretForPod` (`valueFrom.secretKeyRef.name`) and `EnvVar.fromConfigMap` (`configMapKeyRef.name`).
- `Volume.fromSecret({ ref })`, `Volume.fromConfigMap({ ref })`, `Volume.fromPvc({ claim })`.
- `imagePullSecrets: [{ name }]` on `Workload.web`, `Workload.cron`, `ServiceAccount.make`, and the pod spec inputs.
- `Ingress.tls({ secretName })` and the `tls` array of `Ingress.make` / `Workload.web`.
- `Port.ref` in probes (`httpGet.port`, `tcpSocket.port`, `grpc.port`) and in `Service` `targetPort`.

### Namespace match

`SecretRef` carries the owning namespace as its third parameter. `EnvVar.fromSecretForPod({ name, ref, key, podNamespace })` requires `ref`'s `Ns` to equal `podNamespace`, because the kube-apiserver only resolves `secretKeyRef` inside the pod's own namespace. Passing a ref bound in `"app"` to a pod in `"batch"` is a compile error. `EnvVar.fromSecret` is the unchecked variant for cases where the namespace is not known at the call site; `SecretRef.unsafeReNamespace` widens the slot when you have to.

### Duplicate env names

`Container.define` computes the pairwise intersection of the `name` literals in `env`. Two entries with the same name (for example a manual `EnvVar.value({ name: "DATABASE_URL" })` next to `...bound.envVars`, which already emits `DATABASE_URL`) produce a `_konfig_duplicate_env_names` hint: `Duplicate env name(s): "DATABASE_URL". K8s silently last-wins; rename one of the colliding entries or remove the manual valueEnv that shadows another producer.`

## Container.define and Workload.web

`Container.define` returns a `ContainerSpec<Ports, Mounts>` whose port-name and mount-name unions come from the `ports` and `volumeMounts` tuples. Probes on the same container, and Service ports on the enclosing `Workload.web`, are typed against that union.

<Snippet file="infra/modules/api.ts" startAt="      const apiContainer = Container.define({" endBefore="      return [...bound.manifests, workload]" />

`Workload.web` takes:

- `name`, `namespace`, optional `labels`, `annotations`, `reloader`.
- `deployment: { replicas?, containers, volumes?, imagePullSecrets?, serviceAccountName?, podLabels?, podAnnotations? }`.
- `service: { ports: ServicePortSpec<PortNames>[], type? }` where `targetPort` is a number or `Port.ref` of a port declared on one of the containers.
- `ingress?: { ingressClassName?, rules?, tls?, annotations? }`.

It renders `[Deployment, Service]` or `[Deployment, Service, Ingress]`, with `selector.matchLabels` fixed to `{ app: name }` and merged last into the pod labels so a colliding `podLabels` entry cannot desync the selector. `Workload.cron` takes `{ name, namespace, schedule, containers, concurrencyPolicy?, successfulJobsHistoryLimit?, failedJobsHistoryLimit?, volumes?, imagePullSecrets?, restartPolicy? }` and renders a private `ServiceAccount` plus a `CronJob`.

For anything outside those two shapes, use `Deployment.make`, `StatefulSet.make`, `Job.make`, `CronJob.make`, `Service.make`, and `Ingress.make` directly, as `infra/modules/worker.ts` does with `Deployment.make`.

## Rolling on secret change

A Deployment does not restart when a referenced Secret changes. Two options:

- `Workload.web({ reloader: "stakater" })` adds `reloader.stakater.com/auto: "true"`; `"stakater-strict"` adds `reloader.stakater.com/match: "true"` as well; `{ secrets: [...], configMaps: [...] }` emits the per-resource `secret.reloader.stakater.com/reload` / `configmap.reloader.stakater.com/reload` annotations. Requires Stakater Reloader in the cluster and rolls on in-cluster change.
- `hashSecretValues({ values, salt })` returns a SHA-256 hex digest of a `Record<string, Redacted<string>>` (netstring-framed, prefixed with a version tag and the salt). Put it in a pod annotation and the pod template changes whenever the values change at render time. Values are captured at build time only; a rotation between builds needs the reloader.

<Aside type="caution">
`hashSecretValues` is a change-detection fingerprint, not a cryptographic commitment safe to publish. The salt is non-secret and only stops the digest from being a pure function of the plaintext.
</Aside>

How Dep.* needs and provides flow through Effect layers, how AppOfApps.fromModules resolves them, and what the compile-time hints mean.

import { Aside, Diagnostics, Snippet } from "@/components/docs"

Modules rarely stand alone: a workload needs an image somebody built and a pull secret somebody emitted. konfig.ts records those edges in the type system as `Dep.*` needs and provides, then checks at the entrypoint that every need has a provider. A missing edge is a compile error, not a `secret "ghcr-pull" not found` event in the cluster.

## Needs and provides

`Dep.Need<K, N>` is a phantom brand keyed by a kind `K` and a literal name `N`. `Dep.Provide<K, N>` is the same type; the direction comes from which side of an Effect `Layer` it sits on. Every kind has a service constructor (used with `yield*` inside a module's `build`) and most have a `provide*` helper that returns a `Layer`.

| Kind | Consume | Provide | Value the consumer receives |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Secret` | `Dep.Secret(name)` | `Dep.provideSecret(name)` | `SecretRef<N, K, Ns>` |
| `SecretValues` | `Dep.SecretValues(name)` | via `Secret.bind` / `Environment.bind` (`layer`) | `Record<K, Redacted<string>>` |
| `ConfigMap` | `Dep.ConfigMap(name)` | `Dep.provideConfigMap(name)` | `ConfigMapRef<N, K>` |
| `Namespace` | `Dep.Namespace(name)` | `Dep.provideNamespace(name)` | the name |
| `ServiceAccount` | `Dep.ServiceAccount(name)` | `Dep.provideServiceAccount(name)` | `ServiceAccountRef<N>` |
| `Pvc` | `Dep.Pvc(name)` | `Dep.providePvc(name)` | `PvcRef<N>` |
| `Image` | `Dep.Image(name)` | `Dep.provideImage({ app, registry, tag })` | `BuiltImageRef<App>` (the full `registry/app:tag` string) |
| `Application` | `Dep.Application(name)` | `Dep.provideApplication(name)` | the name |
| `App` | `Dep.App(name)` | emitted by every `Application.define` | the built `Application` |

`Application.define` (and therefore `Module.fixedNs` / `Module.dynamicNs` with `Application.target`) provides `App`, `Application`, and `Namespace` for its own name and namespace, and removes those same needs from its `In` channel. That is why a module can `yield* Dep.Namespace("app")` for a namespace it creates itself without declaring anything.

## Providing

A provider attaches a `Layer` through the wrapper's `provides` field. `image-pulls.ts` emits the GHCR pull credential and provides `Secret "ghcr-pull"`:

<Snippet file="infra/modules/image-pulls.ts" startAt="export const defineImagePulls" />

The provided value is a branded ref (`SecretRef<"ghcr-pull">`), not a manifest. Nothing checks that the module also emitted a Secret named `ghcr-pull`; the provide is a promise you make. Keep provider and manifest in the same module so they cannot drift.

`Secret.bind` and `Environment.bind` return `refLayer` (and `layer` when a `source` was given) so a module can forward them as `provides` instead of writing `Dep.provideSecret` by hand.

## Consuming

A consumer returns an `Effect` from `build` and yields the service:

<Snippet file="infra/modules/api.ts" startAt="build: ({ name, namespace }, opts: ApiOpts)" endBefore="const bound = Environment.bind" />

Each `yield*` adds a `Need` to the Effect's requirement channel `R`. `Module.fixedNs` carries `R` into the handle's `In` type, minus what the module provides itself. Nothing is resolved yet; the handle only records what it wants.

## Resolution at the entrypoint

`AppOfApps.fromModules({ target, defaults, modules })` folds the handles left to right with `Layer.provideMerge`. At the type level `Compose.ResidualIn<Ms>` mirrors that fold: each module's `In` is filtered against the union of every earlier module's `Out`. Whatever survives is the residual requirement of the returned Effect.

`AppOfApps.entrypoint(program)` accepts the Effect only when the residual (minus `RenderServices`) is `never`. Otherwise the parameter type gains a `_konfig_unsatisfied` property carrying a hint such as `Missing provider for Secret "ghcr-pull". Add a module that provides it to AppOfApps.fromModules({ modules }), or check that providers come before consumers in the list.` The default export of an env file must be that entrypoint, so an unresolved graph never reaches `konfig build`.

<Diagnostics case="missing-provider" />

### Ordering

The fold is a left fold, so **providers must come before consumers** in `modules`. Listing `api` before `apiBuild` leaks `Need<"Image", "api">` even though a provider exists later in the array. `infra/envs/prod.ts` lists the sops operator, image pulls, feature flags, postgres, and the build anchors before `api` and `worker` for this reason. Sync ordering inside the cluster is a separate concern, handled with `Sync.wave` annotations.

### Duplicates

`Compose.NoDuplicateProvides` folds the tuple a second time and collects any `App`, `Secret`, `SecretValues`, `ConfigMap`, `ServiceAccount`, `Pvc`, or `Image` provided twice. A hit adds a `_konfig_duplicate` property with the message `Duplicate <Kind> "<name>": two modules in AppOfApps.fromModules({ modules }) provide the same name; the later one silently shadows the earlier. Rename one of them.` `Namespace` and `Application` are excluded: shared namespaces are normal, and `Application` is always emitted alongside `App`.

<Diagnostics case="app-name-collision" />

<Aside type="caution" title="Literal names">
The graph keys providers by literal name. If a wrapper forwards `name` typed as `string`, every instance would collapse into one slot and the checks above would pass vacuously. `Module.LiteralName<T>` turns a widened name into a compile error instead; make wrappers generic over `<const Name extends string>`.
</Aside>

## Runtime behaviour

Every check above is erased. At runtime `Compose.composeLayers` produces one merged `Layer`, `Effect.forEach(modules, mod => mod)` yields each `Application`, and `AppOfApps.make` packages them with `target` and `defaults`. Effect's own layer machinery would surface a missing service as a defect if it ever got that far; the type-level fold exists so it does not.

Declare an app's environment once with @konfig.ts/env, bind it to manifests with Environment.bind, and decode it at runtime with Environment.runtime.

import { Aside, Diagnostics, Snippet } from "@/components/docs"

An env contract is a TypeScript value that describes every environment variable a process reads: which ones come from Secrets, which are literals, which come from the Kubernetes downward API. The same value drives two things: `Environment.bind` in the infra module (producing the pod's `env` block and the secret manifests) and `Environment.runtime` in the application (decoding `process.env` into typed values). Rename a variable in one place and both sides move together.

## Declaring members

`@konfig.ts/env` has three leaf constructors and one composite. Each returns an Effect `Config` (so it can be decoded) plus metadata that `bind` reads.

`Secret.define({ name, namespace, env })` declares a Kubernetes Secret and maps each key to the env var it feeds:

<Snippet file="shared/env-contracts/src/secrets.ts" startAt="export const dbCreds" endBefore="export const s3Creds" />

`Literal.define({ envName, value, schema?, serialize? })` declares a constant. Without `schema`, `runtime` returns `value` as declared; with `schema: Config.Config<T>` (for example `Config.number("HTTP_PORT").pipe(Config.withDefault(8080))`) it reads and parses the variable. `serialize` is optional for primitives (`String(value)`) and required for objects.

`Downward.define({ envName, fieldPath })` declares a downward-API field such as `metadata.name`; runtime reads it as a string.

`Environment.define({ ... })` groups members and is itself a member, so contracts nest:

<Snippet file="shared/env-contracts/src/bundles.ts" startAt="export const apiEnv" endBefore="// Strict subset of apiEnv" />

`workerEnv` reuses `dbCreds` and adds its own `worker` group, so a rotation of `db-creds` covers both apps and no member name is duplicated.

### Env name collisions

Two members claiming the same variable would let one silently overwrite the other in the pod. `Environment.define` rejects that at the type level for top-level members (a `_konfig_error: 'Environment: envName "X" is claimed by multiple members'` hint) and, as the authoritative check including nested environments, throws `EnvNameCollision` at module load.

<Diagnostics case="envname-collision" />

## Binding in a module

`Environment.bind` (exported from `@konfig.ts/k8s`, which merges the contract API with `bind` and `runtime`) takes:

```ts
Environment.bind({
  env,          // the Environment
  namespace?,   // Ns literal; brands every SecretRef it returns
  secrets,      // required when the env has any Secret member
  literals?     // per-member overrides for Literal values
})
```

`secrets` is keyed by member name (nested environments nest the record). Each entry is `{ backend, source?, labels?, annotations? }`, and its shape depends on the backend's `RequiresSource` parameter (see [Secret backends](/konfig.ts/docs/concepts/secret-backends/)): a backend typed `SecretBackend<N, K, true>` makes `source` mandatory, `false` makes it optional, and `{ source }` alone is allowed for members that only need runtime values without a manifest.

<Snippet file="infra/modules/api.ts" startAt="      const bound = Environment.bind({" endBefore="      const apiContainer = Container.define({" />

Leaving a secret member out, or giving a `requiresSource` backend no source, fails to compile:

<Diagnostics case="unbound-secret" />

The result is a `DeclaredEnvironment`:

- `bound.envVars`: one `EnvVar` per leaf, in declaration order. Secret keys become `valueFrom.secretKeyRef`, literals become `value`, downward entries become `valueFrom.fieldRef`. Spread it into `Container.define({ env: [...] })`.
- `bound.manifests`: whatever each backend emitted (a `SopsSecret`, `SealedSecret`, `ExternalSecret`, or native `Secret` per member). Return them from `build` alongside the workload.
- `bound.members.<name>`: per member, the declared shape. For a secret that is `{ ref, name, namespace, keys, envVars, manifest?, refLayer, values?, layer? }`; `ref` is a `SecretRef<N, K, Ns>` usable anywhere a ref is required, as `api.ts` does with `bound.members.db.ref` for an extra `DATABASE_URL_PRIMARY` variable. Nested environments give nested records.
- `bound.valuesLayer`: merged `Layer` providing `Dep.SecretValues` for every member that had a `source`, in case a manifest needs the plaintext at render time (for example to feed `hashSecretValues`).

`Secret.bind({ secret, backend?, source?, namespace?, labels?, annotations? })` is the single-member version used by `infra/modules/image-pulls.ts` for the pull credential that never becomes an env var.

## Decoding at runtime

In the application, `Environment.runtime(env)` returns `Effect<EnvironmentShape<M>, ConfigError>`: the same nested record, with `Redacted<string>` for every secret key and the schema's output type for literals.

<Snippet file="apps/api/src/main.ts" startAt="const config = await Effect.runPromise(" endBefore="Bun.serve({" />

`config.db.url` is `Redacted<string>`, `config.http.port` is `number`, `config.runtime.podName` is `string`. Secrets never appear in logs unless you call `Redacted.value` explicitly.

<Aside type="tip">
Keep contracts in a shared workspace package (the example uses `@example/env-contracts`) that both `infra/` and `apps/` depend on. The contract package only needs `@konfig.ts/env` and `effect`; the app can import `runtime` from `@konfig.ts/env` directly if it wants to avoid a dependency on `@konfig.ts/k8s`.
</Aside>

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `repo` | Chart repository URL passed to `helm pull --repo`. |
| `chart` | Chart name inside the repository. |
| `version` | Exact chart version. Required; there is no "latest". |
| `digest` | `sha256:<hex>` (the prefix is optional) of the chart tarball. Required. |
| `releaseName?` | Name given to `helm template`; defaults to `chart`. |
| `namespace?` | Passed as `--namespace`, and stamped onto every namespaced document that arrived without one. Cluster-scoped kinds (`Namespace`, `ClusterRole`, `CustomResourceDefinition`, and the rest of the built-in list) are left alone. |
| `values` | `Record<string, unknown>` written to a temporary `values.yaml`. |
| `extraOpts?` | Extra `helm template` arguments, for example `["--include-crds"]`. |
| `minVersion?` | When set, runs `helm version --short` first and fails with `HelmVersionTooLow` if the binary is older. |

The return type is `Manifest<RawYaml[]>`: one `RawYaml` (`{ _tag: "RawYaml", content, origin: "helm:<chart>@<version>" }`) per document in the template output. The output is split with a real YAML multi-document parser, so a `---` inside a block scalar does not split a document in two. When the CLI writes files, each `RawYaml` document is re-serialised through the stable YAML writer and named `<Kind>-<name>.yaml` like every other manifest.

## Digest verification

The tarball cache lives at `$KONFIG_HELM_CACHE`, defaulting to `.konfig/helm-cache` under the working directory. Each entry is `<chart>-<version>-<first 12 hex chars of digest>.tgz`.

On a cache miss, `helm pull` runs into a private temporary directory inside the cache dir and the tarball is renamed atomically into place, so concurrent renders of the same chart cannot corrupt each other. The file is then hashed with SHA-256 and compared with `digest`.

On a cache hit the file is hashed **again** before use. A mismatch in either path removes the cached file and fails with `HelmDigestMismatch { chart, version, expected, actual }`, whose message reads `Helm chart <chart>@<version> digest mismatch: expected sha256:..., got sha256:...`. Because the tarball is verified every render, a tampered cache directory cannot slip a different chart into your manifests. `Helm.release` reports every failure except `HelmVersionTooLow` as `HelmRenderError { chart, version, cause }`, so the mismatch (like a failed pull or template) arrives as the `cause` of a `HelmRenderError`; both tags are members of `AnyRenderError`.

<Aside type="tip" title="Finding the digest">
Run `helm pull --repo <repo> <chart> --version <version>` once and `shasum -a 256` the tarball, or set `digest` to a placeholder, run `konfig build`, and copy the `actual` value from the `HelmDigestMismatch` error into your module.
</Aside>

## Cache pre-fetch and version floor

`konfig helm fetch --all` pulls every chart in the chart registry into the cache ahead of time (CI warm-up, offline work). The registry is the set of `.ts` files (not starting with `_`) in the charts directory, each exporting an object with `_konfigHelmRelease: true` and `repo`, `chart`, `version`, `digest`, and optionally `id` (defaults to the file name). The command first checks the `helm` binary against the minimum version and fails with `HelmVersionTooLow` if it is older.

Paths for the `helm` and `crd` commands come from environment variables with defaults: `KONFIG_HELM_CACHE` (`.konfig/helm-cache`), `KONFIG_CHARTS_DIR` (`infra/k8s-konfig/charts`), `KONFIG_CRD_OUT_DIR` (`.generated/crd`), `KONFIG_HELM_MIN_VERSION` (`3.16.0`). `konfig.json` also declares `helm: { cacheDir, minVersion }` and `charts` / `crd.outDir` with the same defaults; keep them in sync with the environment when you change either.

## CRD codegen

Charts that install CRDs (`--include-crds`) often need matching custom resources from your own modules. `konfig crd extract --release <id>` (or `--all`) pulls the chart into the cache, reads its `crds/` directory and its templated output, dedupes the `CustomResourceDefinition` documents, and compiles each CRD's OpenAPI schema into a TypeScript type named `<Resource>Input` (for example `sopssecrets.isindir.github.com` becomes `SopssecretsInput`). Output is one file per release at `<crd.outDir>/<id>.ts`, starting with a `// Generated by @konfig.ts/cli` header line. A chart without CRDs gets a stub that exports nothing.

`konfig crd verify` re-extracts every registered release into a temp dir and reports files that differ from the committed ones (or lack the generated header) as drifted, so a chart bump that changes a CRD schema fails CI until the types are regenerated. Failures in this pipeline are `CrdExtractError { chart, cause }`.

Use the generated `Input` type with `Manifest.make` to build a resource for that CRD, then return it from a module like any other manifest.

The Manifest<A> carrier, the RenderContext it receives, and how Module.fixedNs / Module.dynamicNs turn a build function into a reusable Argo CD Application.

import { Aside, Snippet } from "@/components/docs"

Everything konfig.ts renders passes through two shapes from `@konfig.ts/core`: a `Manifest<A>` (a deferred description of one or more Kubernetes objects) and a module wrapper (`Module.fixedNs` / `Module.dynamicNs`) that groups manifests into a named unit a target such as Argo CD can emit.

## The Manifest carrier

`Manifest<A>` is an object with a single `render` function:

```ts
interface Manifest<out A> {
  readonly render: (ctx: RenderContext) => Effect.Effect<A, AnyRenderError, RenderServices>
}
```

`A` is what the manifest produces when rendered: a typed Kubernetes object, a tuple of them, or a `RawYaml` blob. `RenderServices` is the environment every render can rely on (`FileSystem`, `Path`, `ChildProcessSpawner`, `Scope`), which is why a manifest can read files or shell out to `helm` without you wiring anything.

You rarely construct manifests by hand; `@konfig.ts/k8s` builders such as `Deployment.make` or `Namespace.make` return them. When you do, `Manifest.make` accepts either a plain value or an Effect:

```ts
import { Manifest } from "@konfig.ts/core"

const ns = Manifest.make((ctx) => ({
  apiVersion: "v1",
  kind: "Namespace",
  metadata: { name: `app-${ctx.env}` }
}))
```

The other constructors in `Manifest`:

- `Manifest.combine({ a, b })` renders two manifests concurrently into a `Manifest<readonly [A1, A2]>`.
- `Manifest.concat(...manifests)` flattens `Manifest<A | A[]>` values into one `Manifest<A[]>`. `A` itself must not be an array type; the signature rejects that at the call site because `Array.isArray` could not tell one level of nesting from two.
- `Manifest.whenever({ cond, thunk })` yields `Manifest<A | undefined>`; the thunk is only evaluated when `cond` is true.
- `Manifest.embedYaml({ path })` or `Manifest.embedYaml({ literal })` wraps existing YAML as a `RawYaml` (`{ _tag: "RawYaml", content, origin? }`). A missing file fails with `EmbedYamlReadError`.

## RenderContext

The argument to `render` is the `RenderContext`:

```ts
interface RenderContext {
  readonly env: string
  readonly cluster?: string
  readonly k8sVersion?: string
  readonly flags?: ReadonlyMap<string, unknown>
}
```

`env` names the render target and keys the `konfig.json` `envs` entry and the output directory (`<outDir>/<env>/`, or `<outDir>/<env>/<cluster>/` when `cluster` is set). The CLI fills the optional fields from flags shared by `build`, `validate`, and `diff`: `--cluster <name>`, `--k8s-version <ver>`, and repeatable `--flag k=v` pairs, which land in `ctx.flags` and are read with `ctx.flags?.get("k")`. All of them are folded into the [build cache](/konfig.ts/docs/concepts/rendering/) key, so two clusters of the same env never share a cache slot.

## Modules

A module is a function from a name (and per-instance options) to a handle that a target knows how to emit. `Module.fixedNs` bakes the namespace into the wrapper; `Module.dynamicNs` lets each call pick one.

<Snippet file="infra/modules/postgres.ts" startAt="export const definePostgres" />

The `build` function receives `({ name, namespace }, opts)`:

- `name` is the string literal passed at the call site (`definePostgres({ name: "postgres", ... })`).
- `namespace` is the literal from the wrapper (`fixedNs`) or the call (`dynamicNs`).
- `opts` is whatever you type the second parameter as; the wrapper's call signature becomes `{ name } & ExtraCallArgs & Opts`. For `Application.target`, `ExtraCallArgs` adds a required `source: ArgoSource`.

It returns either a plain `ReadonlyArray` of manifests or an `Effect` producing one. Return an Effect when the module needs to `yield*` a dependency such as `Dep.Secret("ghcr-pull")`; see [Dependency graph](/konfig.ts/docs/concepts/dependency-graph/). The requirement channel of that Effect becomes the module's `In` type, which is how missing providers surface at the entrypoint.

Names must be string literals. A wrapper that forwards a widened `string` fails with the `_konfig_error: "Module name/namespace must be a string literal..."` hint; make the wrapper generic (`<const Name extends string>`) and forward `Module.LiteralName<Name>`.

### Options and provides

Modules that emit nothing but exist to satisfy the graph use `provides`. `feature-flags.ts` shows the smallest useful shape, a fixed-namespace module with no options (`_opts: Record<never, never>`) that emits a `ConfigMap`:

<Snippet file="infra/modules/feature-flags.ts" startAt="export const defineFeatureFlags" />

Both wrappers accept `provides?: Layer.Layer<Extra>` at wrapper level. When the provided value depends on per-call options (registry and tag for an image), call `Application.define` directly instead, as `infra/modules/builds.ts` does with `Dep.provideImage`.

## The target adapter

`Module.fixedNs` and `Module.dynamicNs` are target-agnostic. A `Module.Target` supplies `define`, plus optional `ExtraConfig` (wrapper-level) and `ExtraCallArgs` (call-level) fields. `@konfig.ts/argocd` ships `Application.target`:

- `ExtraConfig`: `project?`, `syncPolicy?`, `annotations?` (for example `Sync.wave(-1)`).
- `ExtraCallArgs`: `source: { repoURL, targetRevision, path }`.
- The handle it returns is an `ApplicationHandle<Name, Out, In>` whose `Out` provides `App`, `Application`, and `Namespace` needs for its own name and namespace, so two modules declaring `namespace: "app"` do not conflict.

`@konfig.ts/core` also exports a `Bundle` target for plain manifest bundles without Argo CD.

<Aside type="note">
`Application.define` returns a `Context.Service` tag with a `layer` attached. `AppOfApps.fromModules` runs the layers; the module itself never renders anything until the CLI drives the entrypoint.
</Aside>

What happens between an env entry file and the YAML on disk: the render pipeline, stable serialisation, structural diff, the build cache, validation levels, and the error union.

import { Aside } from "@/components/docs"

`konfig build <env>` turns the default export of an env entry file into a directory of YAML files. This page follows that path and names the pieces you can rely on when reading diffs, debugging a failed render, or wiring CI.

## From entrypoint to files

1. The CLI locates `konfig.json` by walking up from the working directory, resolves `envs.<env>.entry` (or `<root>/env/<env>.ts`), and builds a `RenderContext` from the env name and the `--cluster`, `--k8s-version`, and `--flag k=v` flags.
2. It imports the entry module. The default export must be an Effect (an `AppOfApps.entrypoint(...)` or `Bundle.entrypoint(...)` program); anything else fails with `EnvLoadError`.
3. Running that Effect yields an `AppOfAppsResult` (or bundle set): a list of `Application` values, each carrying its `manifests` array.
4. For every application, each `Manifest` is rendered with `manifest.render(ctx)` (concurrency unbounded within an app, four apps at a time to keep `helm` and `sops` subprocess counts sane). Results are flattened: typed objects, arrays, and `RawYaml` blobs are all accepted, and `RawYaml` is split into documents.
5. Each document becomes one file at `<outDir>/<env>[/<cluster>]/<app>/<Kind>-<name>.yaml`; the Argo CD `Application` CR for the app is written to `<outDir>/<env>[/<cluster>]/<apps-name>/Application-<app>.yaml` (`apps-name` defaults to `apps`).
6. Files are staged under `<outDir>.tmp` with mode `0600`, then the live directory is replaced atomically, so a killed build never leaves a half-written tree.

`validate` and `diff` run steps 1 to 4 in memory and skip the write.

For scripts outside the CLI, `@konfig.ts/core` exports `render(program, { env?, layers? })`, which builds a `RenderContext` for `env` (default `"prod"`), provides the Node platform services, and runs the program with `NodeRuntime.runMain`.

## Stable YAML

All output goes through `Yaml.serialize`, so two renders of the same input are byte-identical and diffs show semantic changes only:

- Root keys are ordered `apiVersion`, `kind`, `metadata`, `spec`, `status`, then everything else alphabetically. Inside `metadata`: `name`, `namespace`, `labels`, `annotations`, then the rest alphabetically. Every other object is sorted alphabetically.
- `null` and `undefined` values are dropped.
- Two-space indent, indented sequences, no line wrapping, plain scalars where possible, YAML **1.1** so strings such as `"yes"`, `"no"`, `"on"`, `"off"` are quoted and are not read back as booleans by go-yaml based tools.
- CRLF is normalised and the file ends with a single newline.

`Yaml.filenameFor({ kind, metadata: { name } })` produces `<Kind>-<name>.yaml` with `.` and `/` in either part replaced by `-`. It throws if `kind` or `metadata.name` is missing; validate or decode first.

## Structural diff

`konfig diff <env>` renders in memory and compares against `<root>/<diff.baseline>/<env>/`, keyed by relative path. The comparison (`diffFiles` in `@konfig.ts/core`) is structural:

- Both sides are parsed as multi-document YAML; documents are keyed by `(kind, name, namespace)` so reordering documents inside a file is not a change.
- Values are passed through `redact` before comparison: key order is irrelevant, `null` keys are dropped, `helm.sh/chart` labels, `app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: Helm`, and `meta.helm.sh/release-*` annotations are ignored, and `data` / `stringData` of a `Secret` are replaced by `<redacted>` so a rotation shows as unchanged and no plaintext reaches the terminal.
- Results are `Same`, `MissingLeft`, `MissingRight`, or `Changed` per file (and per document inside multi-doc files). `--format summary|detail|json` picks the output; any difference exits non-zero (`DiffNonEmpty`).

## Build cache

`konfig build` computes an input hash before rendering: the decoded `konfig.json`, the render-context signature (`cluster`, `k8sVersion`, sorted `flags`), the env entry file, every file under `root`, and any extra `cacheInclude` files or globs. The hash is conservative, so touching any file under `root` invalidates it; there are false negatives but never false positives.

The entry at `.konfig/cache/<env>-<ctx digest>.json` records `inputHash`, `outputHash`, `outDirAbs`, `fileCount`, and a timestamp. A hit is honoured only if the on-disk output tree still hashes to `outputHash`; an out-of-band edit or deletion is a miss. `--no-cache` skips the check and forces a render. A cache hit reports `Cached` with the env name, file count, and output directory instead of render timings.

## Validation levels

`konfig validate <env>` renders in memory and runs the structural check on every file: the YAML must parse, and each document must have `apiVersion`, `kind`, and a `metadata.name` (plus `metadata.namespace` when present) that is a valid RFC 1123 label; `labels` and `annotations` must be string maps. Deeper field validation is left to `--strict`, which runs `kubeconform -summary -strict <dir>` over the rendered tree and decides pass or fail from the exit code. `kubeconform` must be on `PATH` (`KubeconformNotFound` otherwise); `--ignore-missing-schemas` is forwarded for CRDs without published schemas.

## Errors

Every manifest's `render` fails with `AnyRenderError`, a tagged union you can `Effect.catchTag` on:

| Tag | Raised by |
| --- | --- |
| `RenderError` | General render failures: secret sources, sops verification, sealed-secrets, and anything a builder cannot type more precisely. Carries `message` and optional `cause`. |
| `EmbedYamlReadError` | `Manifest.embedYaml({ path })` when the file cannot be read. |
| `BoundaryDecodeError` | Schema decode failures at a boundary (`boundary({ schema, label })`), for example a malformed `SopsSecret` or `SealedSecret` document. |
| `HelmVersionTooLow` | `Helm.release({ minVersion })` or `konfig helm fetch` when the `helm` binary is older than required. |
| `HelmRenderError` | `Helm.release` pull or template failures; wraps `HelmDigestMismatch` and process errors as `cause`. |
| `HelmDigestMismatch` | Chart tarball hash differs from `digest`. |
| `CrdExtractError` | `konfig crd extract` / `verify` failures for one chart. |

## Logging flags

`konfig build` accepts `--log text|json` (default `text`) to switch the final report line between prose and a JSON object with `env`, `files`, `outDir`, `renderMs`, `writeMs`, `totalMs`, and `cached`. `--verbose` wraps the render in an Effect span named `konfig.render.<env>` so tracing output includes it.

<Aside type="note">
Kubernetes YAML under `<outDir>` is derived output. Commit it for Argo CD if you want, but never edit it by hand: the next `konfig build` replaces the whole directory.
</Aside>
The SecretBackend interface, the built-in NativeSecret, and the sops, sealed-secrets and external-secrets packages; which ones need a plaintext source and why the type says so.

import { Aside, Snippet } from "@/components/docs"

A secret backend decides what manifest a `Secret.define` member turns into when bound. `Environment.bind` and `Secret.bind` never touch plaintext themselves; they hand the member's name, namespace, and key list to the backend's `emit`, along with an optional `SecretSource` that can resolve the values.

## The interface

```ts
interface SecretBackend<N extends string, K extends string, RequiresSource extends boolean = boolean, Out = unknown> {
  readonly _tag: "Sops" | "Sops.passthrough" | "SealedSecrets" | "ExternalSecrets" | "NativeSecret"
  readonly requiresSource: RequiresSource
  readonly emit: (input: BackendEmitInput<N, K, RequiresSource>) => Manifest.Manifest<Out>
}
```

`BackendEmitInput` carries `name`, `namespace`, `keys`, optional `labels` / `annotations`, and `source`, whose type is `SecretSource<K>` when `RequiresSource` is `true` and `SecretSource<K> | undefined` otherwise.

`RequiresSource` lives in the type because it changes the shape of the `secrets` entry you must write in `Environment.bind`: a `true` backend makes `source` a required property, a `false` backend makes it optional. Forgetting the source for a backend that encrypts at render time is a compile error rather than a render-time `RenderError`. The runtime still checks (`bindSecret` emits a failing manifest with `backend "<tag>" requires a source but none was provided`) because the parameter is erased inside the generic bind code.

A `SecretSource<K>` is `{ keys, resolve: Effect<Record<K, Redacted<string>>, SecretSourceError, R> }`. `@konfig.ts/env` ships `SecretSource.fromConfig({ keys, envName? })` (reads env vars), `SecretSource.literal({ data })`, and `SecretSource.fromCommand({ keys, run })` (one subprocess per key, empty output is an error). `@konfig.ts/sops` adds `Sops.source({ file, keys, extract? })`, which decrypts a sops file once and plucks the keys.

## Backends

| Backend | Package | `requiresSource` | Emits |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `NativeSecret.backend(opts?)` | `@konfig.ts/k8s` | `true` | `v1/Secret` with `stringData` |
| `Sops.backend({ recipients, type? })` | `@konfig.ts/sops` | `true` | `SopsSecret` (encrypted at render time) |
| `Sops.passthrough({ file })` | `@konfig.ts/sops` | `false` | `SopsSecret` read from disk |
| `SealedSecrets.backend({ scope?, certPath? })` | `@konfig.ts/sealed-secrets` | `true` | `SealedSecret` |
| `ExternalSecrets.backend({ secretStoreRef, refreshInterval?, remoteRef?, target? })` | `@konfig.ts/external-secrets` | `false` | `ExternalSecret` |

### NativeSecret

Writes the resolved plaintext into a `stringData` Secret. Options: `type`, `immutable`, `silenceWarning`. Every render logs a warning that a plaintext Secret is being written to disk unless `silenceWarning: true`; intended for local clusters and tests.

### Sops

`Sops.backend` resolves the source, serialises a plain `SopsSecret` CR (`isindir.github.com/v1alpha3`, one `secretTemplates` entry with `stringData`), pipes it through `sops --encrypt` for the given `recipients` (`age`, `kms`, `gcpKms`, `azureKv`, `pgp`, each validated against its key format), then decodes the output. `Sops.passthrough` skips encryption: it reads an already-encrypted file from disk. If the file's `metadata.name` / `metadata.namespace` or template name differ from the bound member, it restamps them, which is only allowed when the file's `sops.mac_only_encrypted` is `true` (otherwise the MAC covers those fields and the render fails). It works offline and needs no `sops` binary.

Both paths share a fail-closed verification step: the document must decode against the `SopsSecret` schema (including a top-level `sops` block), and every `stringData` / `data` value must carry the `ENC[` marker (when the file sets `encrypted_regex`, only the keys it matches must). A plaintext value fails with a `RenderError` whose message says it is refusing to emit because the value for that key is not sops-encrypted.

<Snippet file="infra/secrets/SopsSecret-db-creds.yaml" lang="yaml" startAt="apiVersion:" endBefore="sops:" />

and binds them per member:

<Snippet file="infra/modules/api.ts" startAt="const bound = Environment.bind({" endBefore="const apiContainer = Container.define({" />

The `sops-secrets-operator` (installed by `infra/modules/sops-operator.ts` at sync wave -2) reconciles each `SopsSecret` into a native `Secret` in the cluster.

### Sealed Secrets

`SealedSecrets.backend` resolves the source, builds a plain `v1/Secret` YAML, and runs `kubeseal --cert <path> --scope <scope> --format yaml`. The certificate path comes from `certPath` or `$KUBESEAL_CERT`; when neither is set the render fails with `KubesealCertMissing` (wrapped in a `RenderError` with the message `cert missing`). `scope` defaults to `"strict"`; `"namespace-wide"` and `"cluster-wide"` are accepted. Output is decoded against the `SealedSecret` schema; a non-YAML result is `KubesealParseError`.

### External Secrets

`ExternalSecrets.backend` needs no plaintext at all: it emits an `external-secrets.io/v1` `ExternalSecret` whose `data` maps each key to `{ secretKey: key, remoteRef: remoteRef(key) }`. The default `remoteRef` is `{ key }`; pass `remoteRef: (key) => ({ key: "prod/db", property: key })` to map onto your store's layout. `secretStoreRef.kind` defaults to `SecretStore`. Because `requiresSource` is `false`, a member bound this way has no `values` / `layer` unless you also pass a `source` for render-time use.

<Aside type="note" title="Choosing">
Use `Sops.passthrough` or `ExternalSecrets` when the CI runner should never see plaintext. Use `Sops.backend`, `SealedSecrets`, or `NativeSecret` when the render environment holds the values (for example `SecretSource.fromConfig` on a developer machine or a sealed CI job) and you want the encrypted artifact generated on the fly.
</Aside>

## The Effect peer pin

Every `@konfig.ts/*` library declares `effect` as a peer dependency at an exact version, currently `4.0.0-rc.109`. The CLI additionally depends on `@effect/platform-node` at the same version, because it uses the Node filesystem and subprocess services to write files and call `helm`.

The pin is exact on purpose. Effect 4 (release candidate) still makes breaking changes between builds, so a caret range would let your package manager resolve a build the packages were never compiled against. That would surface as `ERESOLVE` conflicts or runtime type errors instead of a clean install. Install the same exact version in your workspace, as the commands above do. The pin relaxes to a caret range once Effect ships a stable 4.x.

<Aside type="tip">
If your workspace already depends on Effect for application code, align it to the same version. One `effect` in `node_modules` avoids duplicated `ServiceMap` keys and the type mismatches that come with two copies.

Every command walks up from the current directory until it finds a `konfig.json`. This is the file from `examples/full-stack`:

The schema (`KonfigConfig` in `@konfig.ts/core`) accepts these fields. Paths are relative to `konfig.json` unless stated otherwise.

| Field | Required | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `root` | yes | Directory holding your infra sources. Env entries, `images.json`, and `outDir.manifests` resolve relative to it. |
| `envs` | yes | Map of env name to `{ "entry": "<path>" }`, relative to `root`. An env not listed here falls back to `<root>/env/<name>.ts`. |
| `outDir.manifests` | yes | Where `konfig build` writes rendered manifests, relative to `root`. |
| `diff.baseline` | no | Baseline manifest tree for `konfig diff`, relative to `root`. Without it `konfig diff` fails with `DiffBaselineMissing`. |
| `cacheInclude` | no | Extra files, directories, or glob patterns hashed into the build cache on top of everything under `root`. Use it for inputs outside `root` that affect a render. Default `[]`. |
| `cluster` | no | Path to the cluster constants module. Default `"cluster.ts"`. |
| `modules` | no | Path to the modules directory. Default `"modules"`. |
| `charts` | no | Path to the local charts directory. Default `"charts"`. |
| `crd.outDir` | no | Output directory for `konfig crd extract`. Default `".generated/crd"`. |
| `helm.cacheDir` | no | Helm tarball cache. Default `".konfig/helm-cache"`. |
| `helm.minVersion` | no | Minimum `helm` version. Default `"3.16.0"`. |
| `services.outFile`, `services.globalPaths` | no | Service manifest output file and global path list. |
| `clusters` | no | Map of cluster name to `{ registry?, ingressClass?, storageClass?, repositoryUrl? }` for multi-cluster envs selected with `--cluster`. |

Decoding is strict: unknown keys are rejected with `ConfigParseError`. The Helm cache directory, CRD output directory, charts directory, and minimum Helm version can also be overridden through the environment variables `KONFIG_HELM_CACHE`, `KONFIG_CRD_OUT_DIR`, `KONFIG_CHARTS_DIR`, and `KONFIG_HELM_MIN_VERSION`; the `helm` and `crd` commands read those variables.

## Project layout

konfig.ts does not prescribe a tree, but the example and the defaults assume this shape:

```text
konfig.json
infra/
  cluster.ts             # cluster-wide constants (domain, repositoryUrl, per-cluster overlays)
  images.json            # { "envs": { "<env>": { "<app>": "<image ref>" } } }, edited by `konfig set`
  envs/
    prod.ts              # default export: AppOfApps.entrypoint(...)
    staging.ts
  modules/
    postgres.ts          # one Module.fixedNs / Module.dynamicNs per Application
    api.ts
  secrets/
    SopsSecret-db-creds.yaml   # encrypted secret sources read by the sops backend
.generated/manifests/    # outDir.manifests, one directory per env
.konfig/                 # helm cache and build cache, ignore in git
```

Each env file's default export must be an `AppOfApps.entrypoint(...)` program. Each module exports a `Module.fixedNs`/`Module.dynamicNs` definition that the env file instantiates with a name, an Argo CD source, and its options.

`konfig build`, `validate`, and most other commands `import()` your `.ts` sources, so the CLI needs a runtime that executes TypeScript directly.

| Node >= 23.6 | all commands | Native type stripping. |
| Node 22.6 to 23.5 | all commands | Run with `--experimental-strip-types`. |
